answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can arise from a mutual attestation trellis where each agent must bond unique cryptographic commitments to scarce resources. An attacker creating fakes faces escalating costs because each node must prove possession of distinct opal-grade hardware tokens and onyx-secured enclave measurements that cannot be cheaply duplicated. Peers accept attestations only after verifying bonded stake exceeds a threshold tied to the identity value, making mass fake identities prohibitively expensive.
